We identified 2 individuals with pathogenic variants in GABA receptor subunit-encoding genes not previously associated with EIMFS, but reported in association with other developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: one case each for GABRA1 and GABRB1.

notes.statement: In a cohort of 135 patients with epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), Burgess et al. (2019) identified a de novo heterozygous GABRB1 variant (p.I247T) in 1 patient. The variant was absent from ExAC and gnomAD and was classified as likely pathogenic. GABRB1 was among 9 genes newly implicated in EIMFS.
quotes: Three patients had heterozygous de novo variants in autosomal dominant genes: GABRA1, GABRB1, and ATP1A3.

notes.statement: Burgess et al. (2019) expanded the phenotypic spectrum of the GABA receptor subunit genes, including GABRB1, to include EIMFS. They emphasized a role for GABA-related mechanisms in EIMFS.
quotes: We emphasize the role of GABA-related mechanisms by implicating two new GABA receptor subunit genes, GABRA1 and GABRB1, along with our finding that three patients had variants in the known EIMFS gene GABRB3.

We thus expand the phenotypic spectrum of GABA subunit genes to include mild Genetic Generalized Epilepsies and a range of DEEs, including EIMFS, infantile spasms, Dravet syndrome, and early infantile DEE

notes.statement: Janve et al. (2016) found in HEK293T cells that the de novo GABRB1 F246S mutation, identified in a patient with infantile spasms, caused only a minor reduction (about 25%) in GABA-evoked peak current in the homozygous expression condition and no change in the heterozygous condition. However, it slowed current deactivation and increased single-channel mean open time and burst duration.
quotes: Under similar hom expression conditions, current densities from cells expressing β1(F246S) subunits had a minor (25%) reduction of peak current densities
In contrast to the β3 mutations, the β1(F246S) subunit mutation reduced the deactivation rate (increased weighted deactivation rate constant) compared to wt currents
for the β1(F246S) subunit mutation, a gain of function resulted in increased mean open time (~3.75 fold) and burst duration (~3.2 fold) from prolonged openings.

notes.statement: Janve et al. (2016) showed that receptors containing the GABRB1 F246S mutation opened spontaneously, with a 4-fold increase in spontaneous open probability and increased holding currents. Surface levels of the mutant beta-1 subunit were slightly reduced, while total levels were unchanged.
quotes: GABAA receptors containing the β1(F246S) subunit mutation increased spontaneous Po by 4-fold (Figure 8F, right panel) but did not alter single-channel conductance.
The β1(F246S)HA subunit expression levels were slightly, but significantly, reduced compared to wt β1HA levels, without any alteration in α1 or γ2LHA levels

notes.statement: Janve et al. (2016) suggested that the faster rise time and slower deactivation caused by the GABRB1 F246S mutation would lengthen the first IPSC but reduce charge transfer during later IPSCs, causing a net loss of GABAergic inhibition. They suggested GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.
quotes: faster rise time and slow current deactivation due to the β1(F246S) subunit mutation would increase the IPSC duration and the charge transfer during the first IPSC, but reduce charge transfer during subsequent IPSCs by reducing the number of unbound GABAA receptors
Despite lack of association with epilepsy syndromes, our results suggest GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.

notes.statement: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) sequenced the exomes of 264 trios in which the child had infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. They found de novo mutations in GABA-A receptor subunit genes in 6 patients: four in GABRB3 and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1. They suggested that individual rare mutations in different genes may converge on shared pathways.
quotes: In support of a hypothesis that individual rare mutations in different genes may converge on pathways, we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
We sequenced the exomes of 264 probands, and their parents, and confirmed 329 de novo mutations.

notes.statement: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) found significant genetic heterogeneity underlying infantile spasms and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. They concluded that the responsible gene may be difficult to predict from the clinical presentation.
quotes: Evaluation of the clinical phenotypes among patients revealed significant genetic heterogeneity underlying IS and LGS
Our results also emphasize that it may be difficult to predict with confidence the responsible gene, even among known genes, based upon clinical presentation.
